php-flaw-patch-scramble.headline: PHP flaw sets off global patching scramble
php-flaw-patch-scramble.body_md:
A bug in PHP, the programming language behind roughly 69% of websites whose server-side language is known, sent IT teams around the world scrambling this week. Some governments and companies did not wait to patch. They switched their sites off.

The flaws were fixed in emergency releases on Wednesday 21 October. The Dutch government took parts of its online services offline, including the DigiD login system. Finland suspended public-facing government services. Edinburgh council and the BBC pulled some pages, and the Wikimedia Foundation shut down a range of supporting services. The Dutch cyber-security centre said it had not seen the flaw abused. The shutdowns were precautionary.

![The PHP logo](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/PHP-logo.svg/960px-PHP-logo.svg.png)

## What is broken

The problem is two separate vulnerabilities, together nicknamed PHP2Shell. Both allow remote code execution without a login. In practice, an attacker who can send a request to a vulnerable web server can make it run their own commands.

- **CVE-2026-109618** is described as remote code execution through out-of-memory corruption.
- **CVE-2026-109619** is described as remote code execution through stale global state. It involves PHP's session upload-progress feature.

The PHP project scores both 9.2 out of 10 under the CVSS v4.0 system, which is "critical". The affected range is wide: nearly every version back to PHP 5.4, across the common ways of running it, including PHP-FPM, Apache's mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed.

Fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PHP 8.1 and older no longer get official updates. Source-code backports exist for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, but not ready-made binaries. Linux distributions often keep old-looking version numbers on patched packages, so administrators have to check a package's changelog for the CVE, not its version string. Wordfence warned that WordPress's automatic updates do not install the PHP fix, because PHP belongs to the server, not the site.

## Found by machines, known for years

The discovery story is part of why this has unsettled people. Reporting indicates researchers at the security firms Wiz and Calif, and OpenAI's Codex Security team, found and reported the flaws, with AI models doing much of the searching. They worked with the PHP security team on the fix. According to the PHP2Shell account on Wikipedia, one of the bugs was found in August during an OpenAI project, and Wiz compared the severity with Heartbleed, the 2014 OpenSSL flaw.

The out-of-memory problem was not wholly new. The PHP Foundation says a core developer noticed signs of it during an external audit in 2024. No working attack was found then. The Foundation has called the delay in fixing it "a structural failure" of its decision process and resources. It is a small organisation maintaining software that much of the web depends on.

## Exploitation: what is and isn't known

The source summary carried no evidence either way on attacks. The record now shows a mixed picture.

- Amazon's honeypot telemetry recorded an exploitation attempt as early as 17 October, four days before the patch.
- Cloudflare reported early attacks and rolled out firewall rules by default, then saw attackers change their payloads to get around them. Its chief technology officer, Dane Knecht, said: "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up."
- Security firm watchTowr said at 11:26 UTC on 21 October that it saw no in-the-wild exploitation. By 14:19 UTC it reported "active exploitation attempts" against both flaws.
- The US cyber agency CISA said on 21 October it had not observed exploitation. No confirmed break-ins had been reported, and neither flaw was in CISA's catalogue of known exploited vulnerabilities at the time of the reporting.

So attempts are documented and successful compromises are not. That distinction may not last. The disclosure also went badly. News leaked on 20 October, Calif accidentally posted a video of its working proof of concept, and advisories appeared 26 minutes before the scheduled release. The security firm Sansec had expected mass attacks within 15 minutes of release.

Official advice was blunt. Gina Peter Banyard, a PHP core developer, said: "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching/upgrading PHP." The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said that where immediate remediation was not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it could be fully mitigated. The US National Security Agency gave similar advice. Stopgaps exist, such as setting session.upload_progress.enabled to 0, but the advisories say they are not complete fixes.

## The test

The episode shows both strengths and weaknesses of open-source infrastructure. A fix reached the major supported branches within days of the leak, and large hosting and security firms published mitigations quickly. But the long tail is the worry. Anything on PHP 8.1 or older depends on someone applying a source patch by hand, and PHP 8.2 itself reaches end of life on 31 December 2026.

There is also a second, unpatched problem. PHP disclosed CVE-2026-115560 on 23 October and plans to fix it in its next routine release. Its suggested mitigation is again to turn off session upload progress. The next measure of this scramble is whether that release arrives quickly, and whether CISA adds the PHP2Shell flaws to its exploited-vulnerabilities list.

met-markle-letter.headline: Met investigates letter making claims about Meghan's father
met-markle-letter.body_md:
The Metropolitan Police are looking into a letter that makes serious claims about Thomas Markle, the father of the Duchess of Sussex. The letter is unverified. The Duchess has publicly described it as deeply distressing, according to reports from BBC UK and the Guardian.

The reports say the letter contains allegations involving child sexual abuse images. They are only allegations, made in a document whose origin and authenticity have not been established. Nothing in the reporting so far shows that they have any basis, and this article does not treat them as fact.

## What is known

Three points are on the record. The Met is examining the letter. The letter makes claims about Mr Markle. And Meghan has responded publicly, calling it deeply distressing.

Much is still unknown. The reports do not make clear who wrote the letter, who received it, how it reached the police, or what stage the Met's work has reached. A police inquiry into a document is not a finding about the person named in it, and the force has not said that any offence has been committed. Mr Markle is a private individual, and the reputational cost of a claim like this falls on him whether or not it is ever substantiated.

## The family backdrop

The Markle family's dealings with the press have been fraught for years. The relationship between Meghan and her father has been the subject of tabloid coverage, public statements and litigation. That history is why this story will draw attention, and it is also a reason for caution. Where a private individual is named in an unproven allegation of this gravity, repeating the detail adds nothing to public understanding and risks real harm.

## What to watch

The next development is likely to come from the Met, which may say whether the letter is being treated as a criminal matter, whether it has been authenticated, or whether the inquiry has closed. Any statement from Mr Markle or his representatives would also matter. Until the police say more, the one firm fact is that an inquiry exists. The claims themselves remain unverified.

carrick-fernandes-drop.headline: Carrick won't rule out dropping Fernandes
carrick-fernandes-drop.body_md:
Michael Carrick has declined to say whether Bruno Fernandes will keep his place in the Manchester United team. The head coach was asked about it on Friday, before Sunday's Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford. He would not rule out leaving the captain out.

The answer matters because of what came before it. Carrick opened his pre-match media briefing at Carrington with an address of about five and a half minutes, rather than taking questions first. It was emotional by the standards of the genre. United have gone seven games without a win in all competitions. The low point was a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como on Wednesday.

## The address

Carrick used the time to set out what he thinks the club stands for. He did not dress up the Como result.

> "Wednesday was a bad night, and it hurt me to see us play like that. It was unacceptable."

He then moved to the standard he wants applied in the dressing room:

> "Entitlement cannot be at this football club."

He spoke of humility and effort as the club's identity. The BBC's Simon Stone reported the address, and its tone was of a manager who knows his position is under scrutiny.

## The Fernandes question

The backdrop was a messy week. Defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's hierarchy. Fernandes publicly criticised the team's tactics after the defeat in Italy. Both are senior figures, and neither comment was likely to be welcomed by a coach in Carrick's position.

Asked directly about dropping his captain, Carrick gave nothing away. His answer, as reported, was about the group rather than the individual.

> "The most important thing for me is the team, the squad and dynamics in the squad."

He added: "I'll always do what is best for the football club."

Neither sentence is a threat, and neither is a reassurance. That is the point. A manager who wanted to calm things would have said the captain was not in doubt. A manager who wanted to hold the line would say what Carrick said.

## What it signals

It would be a stretch to read this as a decision. Carrick has not said Fernandes is out, and refusing to name a team two days early is routine. The evidence for a message sits in the pairing: an address about entitlement, followed by a refusal to protect the player who had just criticised the tactics.

Taken together, they suggest Carrick wants it understood that no one is undroppable. That is a modest signal about squad discipline, and it is addressed mainly to a dressing room that has now gone seven games without winning.

Fernandes was the standout figure of United's last campaign, so the cost of leaving him out is real. The test is the teamsheet for Bournemouth on Sunday. Whether the captain starts will tell the dressing room, and the supporters, how much weight Friday's words carry.

wade-try-record-newcastle.headline: Wade equals Premiership try record as Newcastle beat Sale
wade-try-record-newcastle.body_md:
Christian Wade has drawn level with Chris Ashton as the highest try-scorer in Premiership history, and he did it on a night when little else in the game was worth remembering. Newcastle Red Bulls beat Sale Sharks 17-3 at Kingston Park in blustery conditions. Wade's 101st Premiership try, in the 49th minute, equalled the mark Ashton set in April 2023.

## A record in the corner

Sale led 3-0 at half-time through a George Ford penalty. The first half was mostly kicking, penalties and defence, and the wind did not help either side. Newcastle chose to take the corner rather than kick for goal after the break, and that decision set up the afternoon.

Wade's try, nine minutes into the second half, came in the right corner. Josh Hodge converted. It moved Newcastle ahead 7-3 and made the winger, who is 35, joint holder of a record many assumed would last far longer.

George McGuigan added a try from a maul, and Hodge converted that too and kicked a penalty. Newcastle won without Sale scoring again.

Ashton, who was working as a pundit for TNT Sports, said of the winger: "He has been on the wing all night waiting for his chance, as he always has done." Newcastle head coach Dan McFarland put it more drily: Wade "knows how to find the try-line as all good wingers do."

## The long way round

Wade reached 100 Premiership tries with a hat-trick in a 34-28 defeat at Exeter about two weeks earlier, which left him one short of the record. The Sale game was the first chance to level it, and he took it.

His route to this point has been unusual. He left rugby union for a spell in American football with the Buffalo Bills, then spent time in rugby league with Wigan, before returning to union with Newcastle. He has said the NFL showed him how hard it is to hold a place.

He has been candid that the record is not the only thing on his mind. His contract expires at the end of the season, and he has said he would like to stay in the North East. "Obviously, I would love to stay on, but I'm not sure what the plans are going forward," he said this week. Many people, he added, assume he came back to break the record, but he says he is focused on making the most of his gifts.

## The result matters too, a little

The win was Newcastle's first of the Premiership season, and only their fifth across four Premiership seasons. Sale had not lost either of their previous two league games. Newcastle have long struggled, so for the club the points mattered as much as the milestone.

## What comes next

Wade's next chance to take the record outright comes next Saturday, when Newcastle travel to Saracens. Whether he is selected for that match is the open question. If he scores, the record is his alone.

eagles-nest-fire-arrest.headline: Arrest after fire at Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat
eagles-nest-fire-arrest.body_md:
The Kehlsteinhaus, the mountain-top lodge above Berchtesgaden that English-speaking visitors know as the Eagle's Nest, caught fire on Friday evening. Police have provisionally arrested one person. They have not said whether that person started the fire.

The alarm was raised at about 21:15. By the time the first crews reached the summit at 21:52, German reports say, the whole building was already burning. Fire brigades from six municipalities attended, along with mountain rescue, the Bavarian Red Cross and police, about 200 people in all. They were still working on Saturday morning.

## A hard place to fight a fire

The site made the job harder. The house stands on a ridge at the top of a narrow mountain road, and heavy fire engines struggled to get up it. Crews had to set up an extra water supply. No injuries have been reported, and rescuers searched the building as a precaution. As far as is known, nobody was inside.

How much of the building survives is not yet known. Officials have not said which parts of the historic structure can be saved.

## What police have said

Police in Upper Bavaria confirmed that they detained one person shortly after the fire began, on a provisional basis, and gave no further detail. The newspaper Bild reports that the person is a motorcyclist who was heading towards the building as rescuers approached. Bild also quotes a police spokesperson as saying arson is suspected. The Traunstein criminal police are leading the inquiry under the prosecutor's office.

The reports are careful on one point. Whether the person in custody caused the fire has not been established, and no cause has been confirmed. A provisional arrest is a holding measure, and it can be followed by a charge or by a release.

## The building

The Kehlsteinhaus was finished in 1938 as a gift to Adolf Hitler for his 50th birthday and was used for Nazi Party receptions. He is recorded as visiting only a handful of times. It survived the war and has run as a mountain restaurant and tourist stop since 1952. Visitors ride a dedicated bus up the mountain road, then a brass-lined lift through the rock, and the season normally runs from May to late October. The building is owned by the Free State of Bavaria.

It has long sat awkwardly between two uses, as a scenic summit café and as one of the best-known surviving buildings of the regime. That tension will matter if the police inquiry finds the fire was deliberate and points to a motive. At the moment there is nothing to say about motive.

## What to watch

The next developments are whether prosecutors charge or release the detained person, what the fire investigators conclude about the cause, and what a structural survey finds once the site is safe to enter. Bavaria will then have to decide whether and how to repair a building it owns.

sport-leclerc-canada-england.headline: Leclerc fastest in US Grand Prix practice; Canada beat England twice
sport-leclerc-canada-england.body_md:
Ferrari finished Friday at the Circuit of the Americas as the only team with an answer for the Mercedes that dominates this season. Charles Leclerc topped both practice sessions for the United States Grand Prix. In the second, he was 0.042 seconds clear of Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes driver who stands closest to the world title.

## Friday in Austin

Leclerc was fastest in the opening session, narrowly ahead of Max Verstappen. He then found almost eight tenths in the second, setting a 1m 35.291s. Behind him the order was Antonelli (+0.042), Verstappen (+0.189) and Leclerc's Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton (+0.616). George Russell, in the other Mercedes, was fifth at +0.744.

Antonelli's gap is smaller than it looks. His seat came loose early in the session, and he spent about 10 minutes in the garage while it was repaired. Russell was also looked at by the stewards for forcing Leclerc off the track. They found "nothing dangerous" and took no further action.

The McLaren pair were well back. Lando Norris was seventh, 1.082s off the pace, and Oscar Piastri eighth. Neither managed a clean lap on the soft tyres.

Leclerc himself was cautious. "The balance of the car was good," he said, but "we shouldn't carry too high expectations going into tomorrow." Practice runs are flattering guides, because teams run different fuel loads and engine modes. Ferrari have also gone eight races without a win, so a Friday lead is something to note rather than build on.

The stakes are on Antonelli's side. Sky Sports reports that he would clinch his first world championship with a win on Sunday, which would make him the sport's youngest champion. Qualifying is at 10pm UK time on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday. Those sessions will say whether Ferrari's pace holds up.

## Canada do it twice

In women's rugby, England's Red Roses lost to Canada for the second time in a week. Canada won 31-22 in Ottawa on Friday, a week after a 24-21 win in Toronto. The Toronto result ended England's 41-match unbeaten run, which had lasted four years.

The two games were part of a three-Test WXV Global Series. A 26-26 draw in Exeter in September came first, so Canada went unbeaten across the three matches. Sophie de Goede, the Canada captain, scored a hat-trick in Ottawa. England's tries came from Maddie Feaunati early on and Emma Sing late. Reports say it is the first time since 2016 that England have lost back-to-back Tests.

England captain Meg Jones insisted the side were "not broken" after the defeat. Her words carry weight because England arrived as the top-ranked team. The Exeter draw, then the Toronto defeat and now Ottawa, suggest Canada have closed the gap rather than caught England on a bad day.

The two stories have little else in common, but both leave an unbeaten reputation under pressure. Ferrari have to turn a quick Friday into a result on Sunday. England have to show that the Red Roses are still the team to beat.

civil-servant-five-jobs-fraud.headline: Civil servant who held five jobs charged with fraud
civil-servant-five-jobs-fraud.body_md:
A civil servant who is said to have held five jobs at the same time has been charged with fraud, and says he was "surprised" to find himself facing the charges. The details come from BBC Business reporting. Amounts, employers and the stage of the case were not available to this desk in verified form, and none of the allegations has been tested in court.

The case reads like a workplace comedy: five salaries, one person, and a working week with too few days in it. The legal question is narrower and less amusing. Holding more than one job is not an offence. Public-sector contracts often restrict outside work, but breaching one is an employment matter. Fraud enters when prosecutors say someone obtained pay by lying — about other roles, say, or about availability — and did so dishonestly.

## The 'surprised' defence

The defendant's reaction is the detail that gives the story its flavour, and it is also a pointer to where the case will turn. Fraud requires dishonesty. A defendant who says he did not expect to be prosecuted is, in effect, saying he did not think he was doing anything wrong. That is a statement of belief, not a defence on its own. Juries are generally asked whether conduct was dishonest by the standards of ordinary decent people, and whether he thought it acceptable is only part of that test.

## The harder question: how nobody noticed

Similar UK cases have surfaced in recent years. Reporting on one civil servant accused of juggling several remote government jobs said the arrangement was uncovered not by line managers but by the National Fraud Initiative, a data-matching exercise that compares payroll records across public bodies. That is the more interesting lesson here. Departments hire separately, run separate payrolls and rarely talk to one another. Remote and hybrid work has made it easier for someone to be a name on several rotas without any colleague ever seeing them in the same room.

Pre-employment checks tend to confirm identity, right to work and references. They are not designed to find out whether a candidate is already drawing a salary across Whitehall. Matching only happens after the fact, and only if departments choose to take part.

## What to watch

The next marker is the court record: the charges, the sums alleged and the plea. Those will show whether this is a story about one man's audacity or about gaps in how the state checks who it is paying.
